intro: Every day the dice roll a premise and a dozen constraints, and the game has to honor all of them. Today's roll was seed 3394538433. Here is each roll and what came of it.

rolls.value: an owl night-shift nurse · tuning · rubber ducks
rolls.became: Owls are awake all night anyway, so Nurse Hoo works nights on a children's ward. A hospital at 3am is full of squeaky things nobody is listening to. A rubber duck's squeak can be tuned, a tuned squeak is a note, and enough notes hidden in the right places turn the whole building into an instrument.

You tune a duck the way you'd tune a reed: drag it back on a tongue-depressor slingshot, listen to the squeak climb as the reed stretches, and let go on a line of the gauge. The duck flies into the prank on the blueprint.

A ward door that goes “shh-boop”. A tea trolley that plays a chord only when it's carrying biscuits. A lift that politely plays “going up” all the way down to the basement. Eleven pranks in all, each one drawn up as a sheet of plans.

The Toy Fund is three pence a night, and a gift-shop duck costs three pence. So Hoo returns abandoned wheelchairs for their one-penny coin-lock deposits, writes strongly worded memos, and accepts ducks from half-asleep children's wash bags.
Bramble Ward, and Matron Bramble: a tall grey heron who signs the Toy Fund, underlines things, and comes out of her office whenever a call bell goes unanswered.

rolls.value: automation you program (an action queue with priorities)
rolls.became: Hoo's clipboard. She does the first ticked chore she can, top to bottom, and only remembers a few at once. Put the call bells first or someone wakes up singing. Wheelchairs run “until 20p”, ducks get bought to “keep 2”: the order is the program.

rolls.value: a mid-game rule change that reshapes everything
rolls.became: The fifth prank is Matron's own chair, which plays a polka at the six o'clock handover in front of the entire day shift. Mortified, she cuts the Toy Fund to nothing and pulls the coin locks off the wheelchairs. Money stops. Everything costs favours now, and without a budget nothing gets replaced, so old rubber starts going flat (♭).

The porters were at handover too. It was the funniest thing they'd seen all year, so the night staff volunteer: bats, hedgehogs and mice you move between Scrounge, Tune, Hush and Cover. Covering each other's breaks is how favours get made.

Hoo drew six lines on her gauge, because the whole-tone scale has six notes. But let go exactly between two lines and the duck honks: the other six notes, the other whole-tone scale. The later sheets have “?” slots sitting between the lines.
Everything is small: three pence a night, a dozen night staff, ninety-eight ducks in eleven pranks. A good night is eleven pence.

About three hours over a few sittings, counted in night shifts. When you come back, Hoo has kept to her clipboard and the staff have kept at it (gently: the ward sleeps through, so there are no bells while you're away).
The whole game is Hoo's plans: the ward drawn from above in white line on blue, every prank a numbered sheet, the gauge sketched on the back of a fluid chart.
Eight colours: two navies for the paper, a slate and a mauve for the shadows, and the warm end (rust, orange, peach, cream) for the ink, the ducks and the light by every bed.

The 3am Polka: oom-pah on tiptoe, a tuba-ish bass on the beat and accordion-ish chords off it, over two augmented chords. Whole tone makes it sound like a dream sequence that's a bit tipsy. It goes very quiet when Matron is on the ward, and every duck squeaks on the same scale, until one honks.
Nobody gets told off for long. Children ask for water, stories and ducks. Hoo says “for inventory” a lot.

rolls.value: one last purchase that costs everything
rolls.became: Discharge morning: unscrew every duck from every prank in the hospital and give them all away. It costs everything you have, every duck, every favour and every penny in the jar.

Pip in Bed 4 asked “is there a duck for me?” on the very first night. The Name-Tag Gun, the Gift Wrap Just in Case and the Bed Chart of Notes were silly purchases at the time. On discharge morning every child goes home with a duck in their coat pocket, labelled, wrapped and tuned to their favourite note. Pip gets the first one, an E. Matron hums.

outro: None of these were chosen; all of them were rolled. The fun is finding the one story where they all make sense.
